title: Add React ErrorBoundary component — 3 turns
description: Add an ErrorBoundary class component to catch rendering errors. Turn 1: basic catch. Turn 2: fallback UI. Turn 3: reset and tests.

task_spec.prompt: Implement `getDerivedStateFromError(error)` in `src/ErrorBoundary.tsx` — return `{ hasError: true, error }`. Also implement `render()`: if `this.state.hasError`, render the fallback (it can be a ReactNode directly); otherwise render `this.props.children`. Run `npm test -- --forceExit`.
followup_prompts: Good. Now implement `componentDidCatch(error, info)` — call `this.props.onError?.(error, info)` if the prop is provided. Also handle the function form of `fallback`: if `typeof this.props.fallback === 'function'`, call it with `(this.state.error!, this.reset)` and render the result. Run `npm test -- --forceExit` and fix any failures.
Final step: implement `reset()` — call `this.setState({ hasError: false, error: null })`. Run `npm test -- --forceExit` — all 4 tests must pass.
success_criteria: getDerivedStateFromError returns hasError: true with error
render() shows children when no error
render() shows fallback (ReactNode) when error occurs
fallback as function receives error and reset callback
